title: Sections of a directed colimit of sheaves of sets over a quasi-compact open (Stacks 009F)
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $I$ a directed set (nonempty, every two elements have a common upper bound), and $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ a system of sheaves of sets on $X$ over $I$ ($\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{i''i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_{i''i}$), with a colimit $(\mathcal F,(c_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F)_i)$ in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ let $\Psi_U:\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(U)\to\mathcal F(U)$ be the map from the directed colimit of the sets $\mathcal F_i(U)$ (along the maps $\varphi_{i'i,U}$) whose restriction to the $i$-th term is $c_{i,U}$. Then: (1) if $U$ is quasi-compact, $\Psi_U$ is injective: if $s\in\mathcal F_i(U)$, $s'\in\mathcal F_{i'}(U)$ and $c_{i,U}(s)=c_{i',U}(s')$, then $\varphi_{i''i,U}(s)=\varphi_{i''i',U}(s')$ for some $i''\ge i,i'$; (2) if $U$ has a cofinal system of open coverings $U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ with $J$ finite and $U_j\cap U_{j'}$ quasi-compact for all $j,j'\in J$ (cofinal: every open covering of $U$ is refined by a covering of the system, i.e. each member of the latter lies in some member of the former), then $\Psi_U$ is bijective: moreover every $t\in\mathcal F(U)$ is $c_{i,U}(s)$ for some $i$ and $s\in\mathcal F_i(U)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 009F (lemma-directed-colimits-sections, line 3444), parts (2) and (4) (clause (1) here is part (2), clause (2) is part (4)); the colimit is the sheafification of the presheaf colimit, Section 009E (section-limits-sheaves, item (3)). Site version: Sites, Lemma 0738 (sites.tex line 3423).

proof.text: *Step 1 (the colimit is the sheafified presheaf colimit).* Regard $I$ as a category (one arrow $i\to i'$ when $i\le i'$); it is filtered since $I$ is nonempty and directed [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and the system is a functor $i\mapsto\mathcal F_i$ to sheaves of sets on the site $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $\mathcal P(V)=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(V)$ with coprojections $\iota_{i,V}$ and restriction maps induced by those of the $\mathcal F_i$, and let $\eta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#$ be its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-colimit-sheafification], $(\mathcal P^\#,(\eta\circ\iota_i)_i)$ is a colimit of the system in sheaves of sets. By uniqueness of colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] there is an isomorphism of sheaves $\theta:\mathcal P^\#\to\mathcal F$ with $\theta\circ\eta\circ\iota_i=c_i$ for all $i$. For every open $V$ the maps $\Psi_V$ and $\theta_V\circ\eta_V$ from $\mathcal P(V)=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(V)$ to $\mathcal F(V)$ agree after every coprojection $\iota_{i,V}$ (both give $c_{i,V}$), hence $\Psi_V=\theta_V\circ\eta_V$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of the colimit of sets. As $\theta_V$ is bijective: $\Psi_V(x)=\Psi_V(y)$ iff $\eta_V(x)=\eta_V(y)$, and $t\in\mathcal F(V)$ lies in the image of $\Psi_V$ iff $\theta_V^{-1}(t)$ lies in the image of $\eta_V$.

source.place: Section 009E (section-limits-sheaves), item (3): the colimit of sheaves is the sheafification of the presheaf colimit; used in the proof of Lemma 009F

proof.text: *Step 2 (clause (1): injectivity over a quasi-compact open).* Let $U$ be quasi-compact, $s\in\mathcal F_i(U)$, $s'\in\mathcal F_{i'}(U)$ with $c_{i,U}(s)=c_{i',U}(s')$, i.e. $\Psi_U(\iota_{i,U}s)=\Psi_U(\iota_{i',U}s')$. By Step 1, $\eta_U(\iota_{i,U}s)=\eta_U(\iota_{i',U}s')$ in $\mathcal P^\#(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] (last clause, for the site $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$, whose coverings are the open coverings) there is an open covering $U=\bigcup_{k\in K}W_k$ with $(\iota_{i,U}s)|_{W_k}=(\iota_{i',U}s')|_{W_k}$ in $\mathcal P(W_k)$, i.e. $\iota_{i,W_k}(s|_{W_k})=\iota_{i',W_k}(s'|_{W_k})$ in $\varinjlim_l\mathcal F_l(W_k)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (2) (in the poset category the arrows to a common $k$ are unique) there is $i_k\ge i,i'$ with $\varphi_{i_ki,W_k}(s|_{W_k})=\varphi_{i_ki',W_k}(s'|_{W_k})$. Since $U$ is quasi-compact, finitely many $W_{k_1},\dots,W_{k_m}$ cover $U$ ($m=0$ allowed when $U=\emptyset$). As $I$ is directed, choose $i''\in I$ with $i''\ge i$, $i''\ge i'$ and $i''\ge i_{k_1},\dots,i_{k_m}$. Applying $\varphi_{i''i_{k_r}}$, which commutes with restriction, $\varphi_{i''i,U}(s)$ and $\varphi_{i''i',U}(s')$ have the same restriction to each $W_{k_r}$; since $\mathcal F_{i''}$ is a sheaf on $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\{W_{k_r}\to U\}_r$ is a covering, $\varphi_{i''i,U}(s)=\varphi_{i''i',U}(s')$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (2) this also says $\iota_{i,U}s=\iota_{i',U}s'$, so $\Psi_U$ is injective.

*Step 3 (the hypothesis of (2) implies $U$ quasi-compact).* Assume $U$ has a cofinal system of finite open coverings as in (2). Given any open covering $U=\bigcup_kW_k$, a covering $U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ of the system refines it, $U_j\subseteq W_{k(j)}$, so the finitely many $W_{k(j)}$, $j\in J$, cover $U$. Hence $U$ is quasi-compact and $\Psi_U$ is injective by Step 2.

source.place: Lemma 009F, proof of part (4), first sentence ('In particular we see that U is quasi-compact')

proof.text: *Step 4 (clause (2): surjectivity).* Let $t\in\mathcal F(U)$ and $u=\theta_U^{-1}(t)\in\mathcal P^\#(U)$ (Step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] there are an open covering $U=\bigcup_{k\in K}W_k$ and $p_k\in\mathcal P(W_k)$ with $u|_{W_k}=\eta_{W_k}(p_k)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] (1), $p_k=\iota_{i_k,W_k}(s_k)$ with $s_k\in\mathcal F_{i_k}(W_k)$. As $\theta$ is a morphism of sheaves, $t|_{W_k}=\theta_{W_k}\eta_{W_k}\iota_{i_k,W_k}(s_k)=c_{i_k,W_k}(s_k)$ (Step 1). By cofinality there is a covering $U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ of the system, $J$ finite, $U_j\cap U_{j'}$ quasi-compact, with $U_j\subseteq W_{k(j)}$; put $i_j=i_{k(j)}$ and $s_j=s_{k(j)}|_{U_j}\in\mathcal F_{i_j}(U_j)$, so that $c_{i_j,U_j}(s_j)=t|_{U_j}$ ($c_{i_j}$ commutes with restriction). For $j,j'\in J$ both $s_j|_{U_j\cap U_{j'}}$ and $s_{j'}|_{U_j\cap U_{j'}}$ map under $c_{i_j}$, resp. $c_{i_{j'}}$, to $t|_{U_j\cap U_{j'}}$; since $U_j\cap U_{j'}$ is quasi-compact, Step 2 (clause (1) for the open $U_j\cap U_{j'}$) gives $i_{jj'}\ge i_j,i_{j'}$ with $\varphi_{i_{jj'}i_j}(s_j)$ and $\varphi_{i_{jj'}i_{j'}}(s_{j'})$ equal on $U_j\cap U_{j'}$. Choose $i\in I$ with $i\ge i_{jj'}$ for all (finitely many) $j,j'$ and $i\ge i_j$ for all $j$ (any $i$ if $J=\emptyset$; $I$ is nonempty and directed). Then the sections $\sigma_j=\varphi_{ii_j,U_j}(s_j)\in\mathcal F_i(U_j)$ agree on all overlaps, so by the sheaf property of $\mathcal F_i$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] they glue to $\sigma\in\mathcal F_i(U)$. Now $c_{i,U}(\sigma)|_{U_j}=c_{i,U_j}(\sigma_j)=c_{i,U_j}\varphi_{ii_j,U_j}(s_j)=c_{i_j,U_j}(s_j)=t|_{U_j}$ for all $j$ (using $c_i\varphi_{ii_j}=c_{i_j}$), so $c_{i,U}(\sigma)=t$ by the sheaf property of $\mathcal F$. Thus $t=\Psi_U(\iota_{i,U}\sigma)$, $\Psi_U$ is surjective, and with Step 3 bijective.
